title: National flu and COVID-19 surveillance report: 8 October 2026 (week 41) - GOV.UK

analysis.time: The report covers data up to week 40 of 2026, which corresponds to the period between 28 September and 4 October 2026. The publication date is 8 October 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The report is focused on England, with data on influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and COVID-19 activity across various populations, including those aged 75 years and over, individuals with weakened immune systems, and specific age groups such as 65 years and over, 6 months to under 65 years in clinical risk groups, and 2 and 3-year-olds.
analysis.event: The report indicates that influenza activity increased and is circulating at baseline levels. It also mentions that ED attendances for influenza-like-illness (ILI) increased and were above seasonally expected levels. Additionally, it notes that the number of influenza-confirmed acute respiratory infection (ARI) incidents in the community was stable compared with the previous week. The report also discusses the status of vaccine uptake for the 2026 to 2027 season.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: Influenza activity increased, with ED attendances for ILI above seasonally expected levels. The number of influenza-confirmed ARI incidents in the community was stable. Vaccine uptake for the 2026 to 2027 season is reported, with lower uptake in certain age groups and risk groups. The report also mentions that findings should be interpreted with caution, particularly in those aged 65 years or older, 6 months to under 65 years in risk groups, and pregnant women.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The report is based on data up to week 40 of 2026 and uses the moving epidemic method (MEM) and mean standard deviation method (MSD) to define thresholds for activity levels. It mentions that some data relating to uptake in pharmacies was unavailable or incomplete. The report also states that findings may be subject to change when additional data become available.

analysis.brief_en: The National Flu and COVID-19 Surveillance Report for 8 October 2026 (week 41) outlines the status of influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and COVID-19 in England. Influenza activity increased, with emergency department (ED) attendances for influenza-like-illness (ILI) above seasonally expected levels. The number of influenza-confirmed acute respiratory infection (ARI) incidents in the community remained stable compared to the previous week. Vaccine uptake for the 2026 to 2027 season is reported, with lower rates observed in certain age groups and risk groups. The report highlights that findings should be interpreted with caution, especially for those aged 65 years or older, individuals in clinical risk groups, and pregnant women. Data on RSV activity remained low, and ED attendances for acute bronchiolitis were below expected levels. The report also notes that some data on pharmacy uptake was incomplete, and the methods used for defining activity levels, such as MEM and MSD, may be subject to future revisions. The surveillance data is based on information up to week 40 of 2026, which ended on 4 October 2026.
analysis.summary_en: The National Flu and COVID-19 Surveillance Report for 8 October 2026 (week 41) outlines the status of influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and COVID-19 in England. Influenza activity increased, with emergency department (ED) attendances for influenza-like-illness (ILI) above seasonally expected levels. The number of influenza-confirmed acute respiratory infection (ARI) incidents in the community remained stable compared to the previous week. Vaccine uptake for the 2026 to 2027 season is reported, with lower rates observed in certain age groups and risk groups. The report highlights that findings should be interpreted with caution, especially for those aged 65 years or older, individuals in clinical risk groups, and pregnant women. Data on RSV activity remained low, and ED attendances for acute bronchiolitis were below expected levels. The report also notes that some data on pharmacy uptake was incomplete, and the methods used for defining activity levels, such as MEM and MSD, may be subject to future revisions. The surveillance data is based on information up to week 40 of 2026, which ended on 4 October 2026.
